$comment: Single source of truth for scope -> stage routing, iteration bounds and failure categories.
Read by scripts/lib/pipeline-config.mjs; every consumer (scripts/run-pipeline.mjs, the
workflow skills, the docs) must derive its routing from this file rather than restating it.
scripts/test/pipeline-config.test.mjs fails the build when a copy drifts.
stages[].kind is the TARGET classification from docs/architecture.md (llm | tool | gate).
stages[].kind says who performs it: llm is the workflow skill itself, tool is a CLI, gate is a
decision with an exit code. stages[].tool names the CLI when one exists.
Ported 1:1 from the SUBCHAINS constant that used to live in scripts/run-pipeline.mjs and
from the scope descriptions in schemas/revision.schema.json. Semantics were not changed.

orchestrator.description: scope the change; open/route the revision
orchestrator.label: route

skillValidator.description: validate the skill pack against the target API
skillValidator.label: validate-skills

visualAnalyzer.description: ratios, anchors, regions from the reference
visualAnalyzer.label: visual-analysis

discoveryBarrier.description: the three discovery artifacts validate — may the plan start (exit 0 clear / 1 held)
discoveryBarrier.label: check-discovery

architectureMapper.description: map regions to primitives + theme tokens
architectureMapper.label: architecture

authoringBarrier.description: plan and manifest validate and every requested asset has a record — may the template be written (--for authoring; render-and-diff runs it before a first render)
authoringBarrier.label: check-authoring

handoff.description: record the boundary: artifact paths + hashes, so authoring starts from disk rather than from the discovery conversation
handoff.label: handoff

testRender.description: compile + render + diff + loop verdict, one call  <- mechanical
testRender.label: compile-render

iterate.label: iterate
iterate.description: ask whether the loop may take another pass (0 ready / 2 revise / 3 blocked)

exact-diff.summary: Binary pixel diff against the parent revision.
exact-diff.rule: render-and-diff --against parent reports mismatchPx == 0 on every page (tools/visual-diff at pixel threshold 0 — the AE == 0 this gate is named after); the metric is quoted verbatim in visual-review, never paraphrased.

region-diff.summary: Region-aware pixel diff against the parent revision.
region-diff.rule: tools/visual-diff/bin/region-diff.mjs --changed <ids> cuts every region out of visual-analysis.json and compares it; any region outside --changed carrying mismatched pixels exits 2. The per-region numbers land in region-diff-stats.json and are quoted into gate.regions[], never paraphrased.

visual-review.summary: Layer-by-layer review against the reference image.
visual-review.rule: Per docs/visual-accuracy-contract.md; APPROVE only when every mismatch is at most MINOR or ACCEPTED_LIMITATION. The page percentage is a signal and never a pass/fail here — a rasterised reference never scores zero — so the location of the difference comes from region-diff, whose per-region concentration ranks where to look.

skillValidation.summary: Skill validation is enforced on EVERY scope, including the scopes whose chain has no skillValidator stage.
skillValidation.onHalt: the render process exits with status 4 (the halt contract the skill validation gate enforces)

$comment: Barriers join a fan-out on validated artifacts, not on files existing. Declared here so
the chain, the skills and the docs agree where the joins are — and enforced by code, not
by a sentence: calledFrom runs enforcedBy and refuses to go on while it is red.

analysis.summary: The first render of a new-scope revision is refused until check-analysis --for authoring is clear.
analysis.appliesWhen: a first render (no output.png yet) of a revision that carries visual-analysis.json — a project on the discovery artifacts. One without them (the examples that predate them) is not held to a barrier it never entered.
analysis.onHalt: render-and-diff fails its discovery step and exits 1 before compiling, naming the artifact that is not done and the command that answers

handoff.summary: The handoff is only written on a clear authoring barrier, so a next phase reading one knows the state it names was validated.
handoff.appliesWhen: the create chain reaches the discovery/authoring boundary. There is no such thing as a handoff that says "not validated": a next phase reading one would have to decide what to do about it, and that decision is the barrier's.
handoff.onHalt: handoff write exits 1 naming the artifacts that are not done, and writes nothing — the previous handoff, if any, is untouched

$comment: The fan-out's input contracts, in one place, so the three prompts do not each restate
them and drift. `node scripts/check-analysis.mjs --contract <worker>` prints one; the
parent pastes that instead of composing a page of prose per worker.
`reads` is the closed list a worker needs. It is short on purpose: in a recorded run the
content worker read authoring-rules.md — 4.7k tokens of GraphCompose authoring guidance —
to extract strings out of a picture. A worker that reads what it does not use pays for it
on every one of its own turns.
`writesVia` is not advice. A worker that writes the canonical path directly leaves it
truncated for as long as the write takes, and a reader inside that window sees half a
document; scripts/write-artifact.mjs stages, validates and renames instead.
Discovery and authoring are separate context lifetimes. Everything authoring needs
exists as validated artifacts once the authoring barrier is clear, and the handoff
records where they are and what they hashed to — so a fresh authoring context reads
five files instead of inheriting a 192-266k-token discovery conversation it cannot use.
Measured on two recorded create runs: authoring+loop was 84% and 96% of cache-read,
the three discovery workers 3.0% and 0.0%.
The boundary is here and nowhere else. The author/render/revise loop keeps one context
on purpose: its passes are corrections to the pass before, and restoring that from disk
each time would cost more than carrying it.

geometry.summary: ratios, regions, roles, flow and pagination — the page as dependencies, not pixels

content.summary: every variable string the reference shows, with hrefs, behind a typed spec

assets.summary: the icons and font families the reference names, as tokens and roles

$authorComment: The author is a discovery worker's opposite number: it runs AFTER the boundary,
in its own context, and it is the one the fan-out's discipline never covered.
A measured run proved why it needs one. The fresh context started at 43.8k and
grew to 333.7k over 131 requests; its first calls were `cat` of the whole
authoring-rules.md, then whole graphcompose-basics.md and layout pages, then a
harness source file, then another project's revision. It released 167.4k at the
boundary and re-accumulated most of it — the same carry cost, one phase later.
`mustNotLoadByDefault` is the part with evidence behind it. It is not a ban:
`escalation` says how to read one deliberately when a narrow tool cannot answer.

author.summary: the template class and its spec provider, written from the handoff's five artifacts
author.escalation: scripts/handoff.mjs escalate --project <id> --read <path> --because <what the narrow tool could not answer>
author.writesVia: the host's editor, in the revision directory

new.description: First revision of a project (revision-001, or parentRevisionId null). Runs the full chain.
$comment: concurrent: stages with no ordering between them. Asset resolution reads only
asset-request.json and feeds neither the geometry nor the plan, so it runs beside the
plan; serialising it behind the plan measured 26 minutes of the median time-to-first-render.
The join is the barrier stage that follows, on validated artifacts.

visual-change.description: The render must look different from the parent (new layout, swapped fonts, new icon set, restyled section). Compared against the reference image.

refactor-only.description: The render must look IDENTICAL to the parent (class rename, helper extraction, data-spec split, dependency upgrade, package move).

data-only.description: A field inside <doc-kind>-data.json changed (email, phone, heading, list item). Java, assets and theme unchanged.

asset-only.description: An entry inside asset-request.json changed (icon set swap, font family swap). Java, data and theme unchanged.

theme-only.description: A token inside the theme bundle changed (palette colour, type scale, decoration glyph, spacing token). Cross-cutting visual effect, so reviewed against the reference rather than diffed against the parent.

$comment: The four user gestures, each an installable skill. Not a 1:1 mapping onto stages:
a stage like visualAnalyzer belongs to more than one workflow, and approve/review run
no pipeline chain at all. `scopes` records which scopes a workflow can open.

create-template.summary: Reference in, template out; loops until ready for approval.

revise-template.summary: Change an existing template as a new revision, under the narrowest scope that fits.

review-template.summary: Measure and judge the current render; opens no revision.

approve-template.summary: DRAFT to APPROVED, supersede the previous, publish the bundle.

$materialMovePercent: Page-difference movement, in percentage points, below which a pass bought nothing.
Two consecutive attempts on one cause that each move less than this are reported as
stalled by scripts/lib/iteration-status.mjs. Evidence, not a bound: it does not end the
loop, because a threshold nobody measured should not be the thing that ends one.
0.25 is a quarter of a percentage point of the page - on an A4 render at 1240x1753,
about 5,400 pixels, which is a line of text moving by two pixels.
